questions.q: The ability of a joint to move through its full range of motion is called:
questions.explanation: Flexibility relates specifically to joint mobility.

questions.q: Running a 5km race primarily tests which fitness component?
questions.explanation: Sustained, continuous activity relies on the aerobic system.

questions.q: The maximum force a muscle can exert against a resistance is known as:
questions.explanation: Strength is the absolute maximum force.

questions.q: A 100m sprint primarily uses which energy system?
questions.explanation: Short, intense bursts of energy do not rely on oxygen (anaerobic).

questions.q: Agility, balance, and reaction time are examples of:
questions.explanation: These depend heavily on the central nervous system.

questions.q: The 'Sit and Reach' test is commonly used to measure:
questions.explanation: It assesses the range of motion in the posterior chain.

questions.q: The ability to perform a movement in the shortest possible time is defined as:
Doing 50 push-ups without stopping is a test of:
questions.explanation: It tests the muscle's ability to resist fatigue over many repetitions.
